title: Two-player game model
question: Which pure-strategy equilibria exist under an explicitly stated two-player payoff matrix?

answers.purpose: Rehearse an explicit calculation before adapting a protocol to real research. These inputs are constructed teaching data, not collected observations.
answers.sample: Fixed teaching fixture, not a sample-size recommendation or a representative population.
answers.safeguards: Synthetic public inputs under the repository license; no participants, clinical validation or research approval implied.
answers.validation: Recompute using the command in Analyze and compare with the frozen output. Inspect invalid-input tests and the domain-specific limits.
answers.review: Self-check through code and known-answer tests; no independent research review.
answers.units: Two players with two strategies each; utility numbers are assumptions.
answers.comparison: Which pure-strategy equilibria exist under an explicitly stated two-player payoff matrix?
answers.outcome: Pure-strategy Nash equilibria in the stated payoff matrix.
answers.procedure: Enumerate all four strategy pairs and check each player’s unilateral deviations.
answers.analysis: Check unilateral deviations or the chosen equilibrium condition and vary payoffs. Report multiple or absent pure equilibria; do not rule out mixed solutions without checking.
answers.sources: examples/game-theory/README.md; documented fixture definition and code.
answers.limitations: Only pure strategies checked. An empty list does not rule out mixed equilibria. No empirical behavior predicted.
answers.interpretation: A worked model calculation only. No measurements or behavior were observed.
answers.disclosure: Teaching material assembled with automated assistance and checked through executable calculations where supplied. No independent review is claimed.
